title: Learning What to Remember: Resource-Efficient Self-Improvement for Lifelong Agents
abstract: arXiv:2610.26453v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Self-improving agents aim to continuously improve their behavior by learning from experience after deployment. However, accumulating and reusing more experience does not necessarily lead to better decisions, particularly when generation, interaction, and memory resources are jointly constrained. Under such stringent constraints, we find that several existing lifelong-memory methods provide limited benefits over simple retrieval or even no-memory agents. This reveals a fundamental challenge for resource-efficient self-improvement: agents must learn not only which past experiences are relevant, but which are actually worth reusing to improve future decisions. When memory capacity and opportunities for reasoning and recovery are limited, retrieving an ineffective experience can consume scarce resources and hinder downstream execution. To address this challenge, we propose TokenWorth, a lightweight feedback-driven memory adaptation frame

translated_title: 学习记住什么：面向终身智能体的资源高效自我改进
translated_abstract: 自我改进型智能体旨在部署后通过从经验中学习来持续改进自身行为。然而，积累和复用更多经验并不一定带来更好的决策，尤其是在生成、交互和记忆资源受到联合约束的情况下。在这种严格的约束下，我们发现几种现有的终身记忆方法相比简单的检索、甚至无记忆的智能体只能提供有限的收益。这揭示了资源高效自我改进面临的一个根本性挑战：智能体不仅需要学习哪些过去的经验是相关的，还需要学习哪些经验真正值得复用以改进未来的决策。当记忆容量以及推理和恢复的机会有限时，检索一条无效的经验会消耗稀缺的资源并阻碍下游执行。为了应对这一挑战，我们提出了 TokenWorth，一种轻量级的、基于反馈驱动的记忆自适应框架……
tldr: 该论文提出了 TokenWorth——一种轻量级的基于反馈驱动的记忆自适应框架，使终身自我改进智能体在记忆、生成和交互资源受限的条件下，能够学会判断哪些经验真正值得复用，从而实现资源高效的持续自我改进。
en_tdlr: The paper proposes TokenWorth, a lightweight feedback-driven memory adaptation framework that enables lifelong self-improving agents to learn which experiences are actually worth reusing, achieving resource-efficient self-improvement under tight memory, generation, and interaction constraints.
